narrative.overview:
A personal food journal read at night: charcoal ground, warm cream light, and the colour of the food itself. The newest memory runs as an editorial spread; everything after it sits in one even photo grid. The map is a separate room with a shop list at its side.

Photography carries the page. UI colour is a signpost, never the show: orange means the thing you can press, olive means the second dish, red is a single dot on the newest memory. Everything else stays quiet. Tokens live as CSS custom properties at the top of styles.css. color-scheme: dark is declared so native controls follow the world.
keyCharacteristics: Orange #ff6129 is the primary action colour; olive #99af67 is the second dish.
Salmon, yellow and red are held back — red is one 8px dot.
Fraunces for headings, system sans for everything else.
No card panels in the grid: an ink-dark rule and air separate entries.

rules.name: One Accent Per Component
rules.body: Orange and olive never share an element. Red appears exactly once on the page.

rules.name: Photos Beat UI
rules.body: If a coloured surface competes with a food photograph, the surface loses.

dos: Do keep dark surfaces dominant and photos larger than any UI colour.
Do keep one accent per component.
Do keep 44px controls and a visible 2px orange focus ring.
Do keep the single 600px and 900px breakpoints.
donts: Don't add glow, glass, gradients, nested cards, or panel shadows.
Don't use red outside its single dot, or put cream text on an accent fill.
Don't invent shops, photos, ratings or prices — the owner supplies them.
